datasets.label: ALMA · debris disc, 1.3 mm
datasets.title: The debris disc of the Moth (HD 61005) in its own glow at 1.3 millimetres, from ALMA
datasets.description: ALMA observed the star on 18 June 2016 at 1.3 millimetres (project 2015.1.00633.S), 44 minutes on source with 36 antennas. What it sees is the dust's own faint heat, not starlight. This is the image the ARI-L project made from that observation for the public archive, shown at its own resolution, 0.52″ × 0.44″ (19 × 16 au), in gray: one band, brightness only. MacGregor et al. (2018) combined this observation with two earlier, more compact ones; their image has 13 µJy per beam of noise, this one 21. The disc is seen 4.4° from edge-on, so it is a line on the sky. Its two bright ends are where the line of sight runs along the belt of planetesimals that MacGregor et al. place 42 to 67 au from the star. Fainter light continues outward; they model it as a halo reaching 188 au, and this image is drawn in full to 125 au, where its north-east side sinks into the noise, and fades out by 170 au. The image has no third axis, so the depth is reconstructed: the disc is taken to be symmetric about its own axis, tilted 4.4° from edge-on with its south side nearer, as Esposito et al. (2016) read the starlight the dust scatters, and the emission of each ring of radius and height is solved so that the volume reprojects to the image. The star itself is the sphere at the centre.
datasets.summary: The edge-on disc of dust around the star in its own glow at 1.3 mm, as ALMA imaged it. Its two bright ends mark a belt 42 to 67 au out.

facts.label: Instrument
facts.value: ALMA 12-m array, one pointing with baselines to 650 m, 18 June 2016: b6-cont

facts.label: Color
facts.value: Brightness only: one band (Band 6 continuum, 223 to 243 GHz (1.3 mm)) in every channel, in the archive image's Jy/beam

facts.label: Midplane measured here
facts.value: Position angle 70.3° (published 70.3°); the east side is 0.98 times as bright as the west

facts.label: Drawn extent
facts.value: 0 to 170 au; the light reaches the noise at 125 au

facts.label: Depth
facts.value: Not measured; reconstructed from the image by axial symmetry about the disc's normal, tilted toward its south side by convention
